MOLECULAR GENETICS LABORATORY REPORT
[redacted location] Medical Center
Department of Clinical Genetics

PATIENT INFORMATION
Name: [redacted name]
DOB: [redacted date]
MRN: [redacted ID]
Specimen ID: [redacted ID]
Specimen Type: Peripheral blood
Date Collected: [redacted date]
Date Received: [redacted date]
Date Reported: [redacted date]

REFERRAL REASON
Diagnostic testing for infertility. Suspected congenital bilateral absence of vas deferens.

METHODOLOGY
Targeted sequencing screen for common CFTR gene mutations
- Direct sequencing of CFTR exons 4, 7, 10, 11, 12, 20, and 21
- Coverage includes 87.20% of pathogenic variants in Caucasian populations
- Coverage includes 47.44% of pathogenic variants in non-Caucasian populations
- Intron 8 polyT tract analysis included
- Sequencing performed using Sanger methodology with BigDye Terminator v3.1
- Analysis performed on ABI 3730xl DNA Analyzer

RESULTS
CFTR Gene Analysis (NM_000492.4)

Pathogenic Mutations Detected: NONE

Intron 8 PolyT Tract Analysis:
Genotype: 7T/7T
- 5T allele NOT detected
- 7T allele detected in homozygous state
- 9T allele NOT detected

SUMMARY
No pathogenic CFTR mutations were detected in the targeted exons analyzed. The patient is homozygous for the 7T allele at the intron 8 polyT tract. The 5T allele, which is associated with variable penetrance of CFTR-related disorders including congenital bilateral absence of vas deferens (CBAVD), was not detected.

This result reduces the likelihood of common CFTR mutations as the cause of the patient's infertility. However, it does not exclude the possibility of rare CFTR mutations in regions not covered by this assay.

CLINICAL INTERPRETATION
The absence of common pathogenic CFTR mutations and the 7T/7T genotype suggest a reduced likelihood of CFTR-related disease. However, if clinical diagnosis of congenital bilateral absence of vas deferens is confirmed, the condition may still be related to rare CFTR mutations not detected by this targeted screening approach.

Approximately 80% of men with CBAVD carry at least one CFTR mutation. This assay covers the most common mutations but does not include comprehensive gene analysis.

RECOMMENDATIONS
1. Consider extended mutation analysis at a specialist CF laboratory if clinical diagnosis of congenital bilateral absence of vas deferens is confirmed
2. Full CFTR gene sequencing and deletion/duplication analysis may identify rare variants not covered by this screen
3. Genetic counseling is recommended to discuss results and implications for family planning
4. Partner testing may be considered if a CFTR mutation is identified in extended testing

TECHNICAL NOTES
- This assay detects approximately 87.20% of CF-causing mutations in Caucasian populations
- Detection rate is lower (47.44%) in non-Caucasian populations
- Rare mutations, deep intronic variants, and large deletions/duplications are not detected by this methodology
- Analytical sensitivity: >99% for mutations within targeted regions
- Analytical specificity: >99%

This test was developed and its performance characteristics determined by [redacted location] Medical Center Clinical Genetics Laboratory. It has not been cleared or approved by the FDA.

Reported by: [redacted name], PhD, FACMG
Laboratory Director: [redacted name], MD, PhD
